summary: Ancilla College, near Donaldson, Indiana, is a two-year private liberal arts college admitting men and women. Founded in 1937 by the Poor Handmaids of Jesus Christ as an extension of DePaul University for training novices and candidates of that order, it began admitting the public in 1966. The college serves seven surrounding Indiana counties and offers associate degrees with transfer agreements to 14 Indiana colleges and universities; its name comes from the Latin word for handmaid or servant.
one_line: Ancilla College is a two-year private liberal arts college near Donaldson, Indiana, founded in 1937 by the Poor Handmaids of Jesus Christ.

Ancilla College was founded in 1937 by the Poor Handmaids of Jesus Christ.
Ancilla College was founded as an extension of DePaul University for the training of novices and candidates of the Poor Handmaids of Jesus Christ.
In 1966, Ancilla College started admitting the public as a private liberal arts community college.
Ancilla College focuses on serving the seven surrounding counties of Indiana.
Ancilla College grants associate degrees in multiple programs.
Ancilla College has transfer agreements with 14 Indiana colleges and universities.
Ancilla graduates may easily transfer to a four-year college or university, especially via these transfer agreements.
The Latin word "ancilla" means "handmaid or servant."
The name Ancilla refers to the college's sponsor, The Poor Handmaids of Jesus Christ.
